text:
anjali: Heads up - CI smallbatch perf spike on nightly after host driver roll to 12.15.2. 99th tail on tiny sequences up ~18% on A100 pools.
rob: ugh, repro-able locally? which job/commit?
anjali: nightly/inference/fastpath-2, job 3124. Repro on kola-rt-a100-2 with the same driver. linked traces: http://ci.internal/3124/trace
mike: can you paste the nsys / perf counters?
anjali: pasted short snippet from nsys timeline (trimmed):
```
ThreadPoller (pid 3245) blocked -> wake 1.2ms later
DispatchWorker (pid 3250) wake-to-run jitter 0.9ms
GPU kernel queue depth reduced, more memcpy stalls
KVcache LRU tail trims increased from 2/s to 18/s
```
rob: KV tail trims up that much -> suspect more preemption of our scheduler threads causing delayed prefetch, leading to early evictions. any kernel logs? dmesg / cpu-hotplug noise?
anjali: dmesg shows increased workqueue_task latency and a bunch of llist warnings around workqueue balancing. Also saw repeated "workqueue: requeue_on_cpu" messages with driver 12.15.2.
gpu-benchmark-bot: CI alert: nightly/inference/fastpath-2 latency regression exceeded threshold (+15%). Full report: http://ci.internal/reports/3124
helen: timeline: we rolled driver 12.15.2 across infra last night as part of infra/driver-roll. Did we change any kernel module flags?
mike: infra change was purely driver bundle, no sysctl toggles. BUT driver 12.15.2 introduced a workqueue scheduler tweak in the kernel-provided module that shifts default work distribution heuristics (seen in vendor release notes).
rob: ok bisect plan: revert driver on a single node and run microbench. anjali can you run a bisect using kube node-level repro?
anjali: started binary bisect: repro down on node with driver 12.15.2; when I swap to previous driver 12.14.9 latency drops back to baseline within 10 runs.
anjali: git bisect of our infra images shows no infra image changes — narrowed to kernel-driver tag installed by packaging: driver-package@v2026-05-12 -> v2026-05-13 (the latter is the bump).
rob: nice. can we capture perf top while running smallbatch? look for ctx-switches, io-wait, and softirq spikes.
mike: attached perf stat summary from the failing node (averaged):
```
context-switches: +43%
cpu-migrations: +30%
softirqs: +12%
cycles: ~same
instructions: ~same
```
helen: that's consistent with scheduler thrashing not raw compute. Would explain increased memcpy stalls and LRU evictions.
anjali: also instrumented runtime: our workqueue spin->park threshold seems to be firing more often; polling threads parking longer and being woken late. Patch idea: force-thread-affinity for the dispatch thread and increase spin duration to tolerate temporary preemption.
rob: I'd rather not hardcode affinity unless necessary. Since this is caused by a vendor change, we should block rollout of the driver across remaining clusters and open an infra revert ticket.
helen: agreed — rollout block. I'll add a hold to the driver-roll PR and escalate to infra ops.
ci-bot: Created ticket #INFRA-9012: Revert driver-package v2026-05-13 across prod pools. Link: http://tickets/INFRA-9012
mike: while infra reverts, we should prepare an internal mitigation: small change in the runtime's polling backoff (PR in progress). It reduces parking frequency and pins the Poller thread to service CPUs. I'm working on a conservative change that can be hotpatched.
anjali: ack. I also added an automated smallbatch regression test hitting 1-8 token sequences in CI to catch this class of scheduling regressions early.
rob: good. can you post the minimal repro command for others?
anjali: repro command (run on node with our runtime image):
```
./perf_test --model tinyseq --batch-size 2 --iters 400 --pin-gpu 0 --driver-skip-check
```
rob: thanks. once infra revert is in, run the test and attach before/after nsight sys snapshots. We'll also add a gated rollout for future driver bumps to run this test.
helen: tagging release leads @infra-ops and @sre. action items: 1) block driver rollout (INFRA-9012) 2) infra revert on staging+prod 3) runtime mitigation PR & canary 4) add smallbatch perf job to driver gating 5) postmortem once root cause confirmed.
mike: quick note: I ran a synthetic which pins dispatch threads to cpu cores and that almost entirely removes the regression in our lab. So runtime fix viable but we still want vendor revert.
anjali: opening perf artifacts and a short writeup on the bisect with command outputs, nsight traces, and the driver-package diff.
rob: :eyes: nice triage. If infra reverts, we should include a follow-up test to assert LRU trims < 5/s and wake-to-run jitter < 0.5ms.
helen: marking this a rollout blocker until INFRA-9012 is resolved.
ci-bot: nightly/inference/fastpath-2 re-run queued on revert nodes — will post results.
(30m later) ci-bot: Job 3127: smallbatch latency back to baseline after driver revert on staging (delta +1.2%). Full report: http://ci.internal/reports/3127
mike: confirmed. Revert validated the hypothesis. I'll push runtime mitigation PR as a follow-up with tests.
anjali: thanks team — will draft postmortem after we close INFRA-9012 and the mitigation PR is merged. :thumbsup:
helen: good work. we'll coordinate release notes and vendor followup to get a scoped fix from driver vendor.
rob: adding a blocker label to the release board and flagging for oncall.
